name: tier1_combined_probe
_comment: THE NULL-POLISH CONTROL'S SCENE, and it exists for one reason: `tier1_combined_review.json`
REFUSES TO WRITE A PNG when a declared lit point comes back dark, and nulling the polish
shader makes three of them come back dark. That refusal is correct and must not be weakened
— it is the guard that stops a capture circulating with its subject outside the light — so
the control gets its own spec instead.
IDENTICAL TO tier1_combined_review IN EVERY FIELD EXCEPT `legibility`, WHICH IS EMPTY.
Same geometry, same station, same width and height. A control frame that differed from the
build in anything but the one variable would not be a control (LOOP-PROCESS §4.2).
⚠ IT IS AN INSTRUMENT SCENE, NOT A REVIEW SCENE, and the distinction is load-bearing here in
a way it is not elsewhere: a spec with no legibility declarations cannot fail the
floor-legibility guard, so NOTHING IS EVER JUDGED THROUGH THIS FILE. It is used to answer a
measurement question — how much of the floor's delivered value is the specular term — and
for nothing else. Any round that captures a candidate through it has bypassed the guard, and
that is the mistake this paragraph exists to prevent.
Reproduce the control:
sed -i '' 's/"polish_gain": 1.0/"polish_gain": 0.0/' \
src/Presentation/assets/tier1_ashlar/MANIFEST.json
python3 tools/tier0_harness/capture_corridor.py --scene-spec <this file> ... --void-ring 1
# then RESTORE the manifest — compose_ashlar rewrites it, but a stale 0.0 in the tree
# would silently null the shader for every later capture in the session.
⚠ AND EDIT THE MANIFEST BY TEXT SUBSTITUTION, NEVER BY A JSON ROUND-TRIP. The first attempt
at this control loaded the manifest with `json.load`, set the key and dumped it back. The
capture came back with EVERY declared point at ratio 0.0000 including the reference — a
whole-frame failure that looks nothing like the change being tested, and would have been
reported as one if the second attempt had not been made a different way.
_legibility: DELIBERATELY EMPTY. See above — this is the whole point of the file, not an omission.
